subject: Post-demo synthesis: Asteria bakeoff — decision-readiness checklist & smoke probes
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@asteriahealth.com>, Tom Castillo <tom.castillo@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo synthesis: Asteria bakeoff — decision-readiness checklist & smoke probes

Thanks again for carving out time today — great conversation. Quick synthesis from our side and a proposed set of lightweight validation steps so your technical/ procurement teams can rapidly compare us to the other vendor in your bakeoff.

Key pain points you reiterated
- Inconsistent latency at peak (especially during morning ET batch runs).
- Cost unpredictability when volume spikes + need to cap daily spend.
- Requirement for an isolated VPC option and BYO-KMS for PHI data.

Goals you shared
1) Move a small, high-volume scoring workload to a dedicated inference pool for 4 weeks to validate latency and unit economics.
2) Confirm feature parity for streaming / function-calls and deterministic reranking behavior.
3) Validate private deploy (VPC) connectivity and KMS integration before legal signs off.

Decision criteria (what you said matters most)
- Latency SLO at 95th percentile for production pattern (< 180ms token gen for the short-choice prompt set)
- Cost per 1M tokens under target budget when batching at observed qps
- Auditability: request/response logs + KV cache eviction hooks
- Rollout safety: automatic fallback to a lower-cap model without downtime

Proposed smoke probes (what we can run in a 1–2 day validation window)
1) Throughput ramp: replay a 2-hour morning spike (your traces) against a dedicated pool — measure 95p latency, tail latency, and error rate. Owner: Redwood (Jonas).
2) Cost delta: run identical batch of 100k prompts at the bakeoff config and report token cost delta vs. vendor-B. Owner: Redwood (Marissa).
3) Feature parity quick-check: compare streaming chunking + function-call round-trips with your puppeted integration. Owner: Asteria (Sarah) + Redwood (Camila).
4) VPC handshake + KMS test: confirm TLS mutual auth and KMS-encrypted key rotation flow. Owner: Asteria infra + Redwood infra.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Sarah/Tom: share a 2-hour request trace and a sanitized prompt set (ideally 500 representative requests) by EOD Thursday.
- We will prepare a one-page POC-runbook and calendar slots for the validation (propose Wed/Thu next week).
- Legal/procurement: we’ll include an initial draft SOW/commit for a 4-week dedicated pool test after technical sign-off.

Attachments: Asteria_Validation_Tests.xlsx (sheet: test-cases), POC-runbook-v1.pdf (stub).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite after we get your trace.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@asteriahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Castillo <tom.castillo@asteriahealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: Asteria bakeoff — decision-readiness checklist & smoke probes

Jonas — thanks for the clear write-up. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For the throughput ramp we can supply a scrubbed trace (no PHI) but it includes user/session ids that are important for cache-hit behavior. Can Redwood confirm you can preserve the session field and not drop it during replay?
2) On KMS: our security team will need a short design doc that shows how key-wrap happens for model keys vs. config keys — can that be part of the runbook?
3) Timeline constraint: procurement needs a 10-business-day review for any SOW with data-related clauses — heads-up that will push the legal window.

We will upload the sanitized traces and a 500-prompt set to your shared Drive link by Thursday COB. Also attaching a short scoring example that shows how we measure tokenization differences between vendors.

Attachment: asteria_scoring_example.csv (attached)

Tom and I are available Thursday 10–11am PT for a quick alignment call if you want to walk through the runbook before we kick the tests.

—
Sarah Kim
Lead ML Eng, Asteria Health
sarah.kim@asteriahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@asteriahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Tom Castillo <tom.castillo@asteriahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: Asteria bakeoff — decision-readiness checklist & smoke probes

Thanks Sarah — quick replies inline and an updated short checklist for legal/ procurement to reduce back-and-forth: 

- Session fields: yes, we will preserve session_id and any given metadata during replay. We’ll document the replay sanitization steps in the runbook so you can verify.
- KMS design doc: adding a 1-page diagram to the runbook that differentiates model-usage keys vs. telemetry encrypt-at-rest keys — will include rotation cadence and HSM integration notes.
- Procurement timeline: understood. To keep momentum we suggest starting technical validation while procurement runs its review; the POC can be governed by an MSA + POC addendum that limits data exposure and preserves a short term. We can circulate a redline-friendly SOW template after the tests.

Updated short checklist (for our runbook front page)
1) Deliverables from Asteria by Thu COB: sanitized trace (2h), 500 prompt set, scoring example (you mentioned).
2) Redwood deliverables by Fri EOD: POC-runbook v1 (includes KMS sketch), test harness, and calendar for 2x 90-minute windows next week.
3) Success gates after tests: 95p latency within threshold OR documented degradation rationale; cost delta report; successful KMS handshake and proof of logs.

Proposed calendar slots for live validation calls: 
- Wed 11/24 0900–1030 PT (slot A)
- Thu 11/25 0900–1030 PT (slot B)

Please confirm preferred slot. If procurement needs additional language up-front, point us to the relevant contract contact and we’ll loop Legal early.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 650 555 0199
